# All-Hands Follow-up — Engineering Org

**Attendees:** Wei (Director of Eng), Yusuf (EM, Backend), Mei (EM, Frontend), Owen (EM, Platform), Hannah (Chief of Staff)

---

Wei: Good morning. We just wrapped the all-hands. I want to use this hour to translate the announcements into a follow-up plan for engineering. Hannah, can you start with the headline items?

Hannah: Three things came out: first, the company is shifting to a single quarterly OKR cycle starting next quarter, replacing the current half-and-half. Second, the new performance review framework is being piloted in engineering for the December cycle. Third, the founders announced a hiring freeze on non-critical roles through Q3.

Wei: Owen, you have an open req for the platform team. Where does that stand?

Owen: It's the senior reliability engineer role. We're at the offer stage — the candidate is interviewing here next week. Is reliability "critical"?

Wei: Yes. Reliability roles are explicitly carved out of the freeze. Hannah, can you confirm in writing? I don't want any ambiguity from finance side.

Hannah: I'll get the carve-out language in writing from the CFO this week.

Yusuf: My open req is also affected — the senior backend role we just decided to hire on. We discussed Casey Liu yesterday in the debrief.

Wei: That offer is already in motion, so it predates the freeze announcement. It stands. But please don't open new reqs without my sign-off.

Yusuf: Understood.

Mei: Question on the OKR cycle change. Our current frontend OKRs span two quarters. Do we re-cut at the boundary or finish the current set?

Wei: Finish the current set. The new cadence kicks in for the next planning cycle. Mei, please write a one-pager for your team explaining the transition and post it by next Wednesday.

Mei: Will do.

Owen: Same question for platform — same answer?

Wei: Same answer. Owen, you also write a transition note. Same deadline.

Yusuf: I can take a similar one-pager for backend.

Wei: Three transition notes by next Wednesday. Hannah, can you compile them into a single document for the all-hands recap that goes out the following Monday?

Hannah: Yes, I'll send the compiled doc to Wei for review on Friday next week.

Mei: On the new performance review framework — what's the engineering pilot look like? Are we doing the full pilot or a subset?

Hannah: Engineering does the full pilot. Forty managers in scope, two-week training kickoff in October. The training is mandatory.

Wei: I'll add the training dates to my calendar and forward to Yusuf, Mei, and Owen as a hold. Hannah, please send me the calendar invites so I can forward.

Hannah: I'll send them to you by end of day tomorrow.

Yusuf: Concern — the training timing is right before the December review cycle. If anything goes wrong with the framework, we'll be debugging it during real reviews.

Wei: Valid. Yusuf, draft a list of three potential failure modes and the mitigations. I'll bring it to the people-ops conversation. Have it to me by next Friday.

Yusuf: Got it.

Mei: One thing not from the all-hands — last week's outage. We agreed the postmortem would be done by today. Owen, where are we?

Owen: Postmortem is drafted. I'm doing the final pass this morning and circulating before noon. Action items from it carry into next sprint.

Mei: Make sure the timeline is clear about the rollback decision lag. That's the sharpest critique I've seen externally.

Owen: It will be.

Wei: Final piece — town halls. The next engineering town hall is in three weeks. I'd like the agenda to cover the OKR transition, the review framework, and the freeze. Hannah, draft the agenda by next Wednesday.

Hannah: Will do.

Wei: Recap. Hannah confirms the reliability-role freeze carve-out in writing this week and sends performance-training calendar invites by end of day tomorrow. Owen, Mei, Yusuf each write a transition one-pager for their teams by next Wednesday. Hannah compiles the transition notes for Wei's review by Friday next week. Yusuf drafts the three failure modes and mitigations for the new review framework by next Friday. Owen circulates the outage postmortem before noon today. Hannah drafts the next engineering town-hall agenda by next Wednesday. Anything missing?

Mei: That covers it.

Wei: Thanks all.
